title: Property software firm adds AI tools for admin tasks
summary:
Property software provider Veco has released four artificial intelligence-powered features within its Ask Veco assistant, aimed at automating administrative tasks for estate and letting agents across the UK. The tools address compliance documentation, supplier invoices, repair reporting and applicant matching.

title: Five sport-focused homes listed across England
summary:
Five residential properties with sports facilities or proximity to sporting venues have been listed across England, ranging from £350,000 to £2.995 million. The listings include properties in London, Kent, Birmingham, Devon and Cumbria.

title: Paragon Bank provides £3.3m for Derbyshire trade park
summary:
Paragon Bank's Development Finance division has provided £3.3 million to Litton Properties for a seven-unit trade park at Markham Vale in Derbyshire. The transaction represents Paragon's first completed deal since launching its light industrial lending proposition earlier this year.

The post Paragon Bank provides £3.3m for Derbyshire trade park appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Specialist lender completes £2.5m multi-property deal
summary:
Hampshire Trust Bank has completed three refinancing deals totalling approximately £2.5m for a single investor group, covering buy-to-let and semi-commercial properties across Yorkshire and Greater Manchester. The facilities covered 23 residential units and two commercial units across properties in Leeds, Hyde and Sheffield.

title: UK property market shows mixed signals in latest data
summary:
The UK residential property market recorded 32,200 new listings in week 41 of 2026, with year-to-date sales volumes down 7.5% compared to 2025. Transaction data reveals 54% of homes leaving agents' books in September exchanged and completed, below the seven-year average of 57.6%.

title: Half of landlords hold rents steady to retain tenants
summary:
Half of landlords in England have kept rents unchanged over the past year, up from 40% previously, according to research by the TDS Charitable Foundation. The study found that retaining existing tenants was the primary reason for maintaining rents at current levels.

The post Half of landlords hold rents steady to retain tenants appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Three quarters of home movers regret information gaps
summary:
Nearly three quarters of recent home buyers and sellers wish they had received more information about properties or locations before making or accepting offers, according to new research from Landmark Information Group. The findings reveal that more than two-thirds experienced uncertainty or delays after offers were accepted.

The post Three quarters of home movers regret information gaps appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Over a third of letting agents fail to display fees online
summary:
More than a third of letting agent websites in England do not display fee information, according to research examining 400 firms. The analysis found 34.5% had no fees page or mention of fees, despite legal requirements under the Consumer Rights Act 2015.

The post Over a third of letting agents fail to display fees online appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Letting agents tighten tenant screening following new law
summary:
More than half of letting agents have increased caution when recommending tenants to landlords since the Renters' Rights Act came into force. The survey found that 51% of agents have tightened their recommendation criteria, whilst 31% of landlords would prefer to leave properties vacant whilst searching for lower-risk tenants.

The post Letting agents tighten tenant screening following new law appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Third of London first-time buyers exceed LISA price cap
summary:
More than a third of first-time buyer purchases in London now exceed the Lifetime ISA's £450,000 property price cap, according to new data from reallymoving. The research shows that 34% of London purchases exceeded the cap in 2026, up from 25.7% in 2017.
